memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and all that
is in them, but he rested on the seventh day. Therefore the LORD blessed the
Sabbath day and made it holy.'" - Ex 20:11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The reason given for the Sabbath is God's own example.

God rested. Not because He was tired; Isaiah says plainly that the Creator "will
not grow tired or weary" (Isa 40:28). He rested because the work was complete,
and He stopped to enjoy what He had made.

That reframes rest entirely. It is not merely recovery from exhaustion. It is the
enjoyment of finished work. There is a satisfaction in stopping that has nothing
to do with being worn out.

Most of us only stop when we cannot continue. We treat rest as maintenance for
more production. God treats it as good in itself.

Notice that God "blessed" the seventh day and "made it holy." Rest was declared
good before any law required it, back in Genesis 2, before sin, before Sinai. It
belongs to how the world was made, not merely to Israel's legal code.

And there is a deeper rest this points toward. Hebrews says, "There remains,
then, a Sabbath-rest for the people of God" (Heb 4:9), and invites us to rest
from trying to earn what Christ has finished.

Jesus said, "It is finished" (John 19:30). Rest is what you do when the work is
done.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you rest only when exhausted, or as something good in itself?
2. Are you still working for what Christ has already finished?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You rested and called it good. Teach me to stop, to enjoy, and to rest in
the finished work of Jesus. Amen.
